name: My Client's Position and Demand
title: My Client's Position and Demand
text:
6. Far from my client being liable to your client, it is your client who is liable to my client in respect of {{counter_claim_description}}.
7. My client calls upon your client to withdraw the said notice and to {{counter_demand}}, failing which my client will take such proceedings as it is advised, at your client's risk as to costs.

legal_basis.note: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
A defendant may set up a counter-claim against the claim of the plaintiff

source: Civil Procedure Code, 1908; Indian Contract Act, 1872
statutory_reference: Indian Contract Act, 1872 - S.73; Civil Procedure Code, 1908 - Order VIII Rule 6A
authoring_note: Whether to make a counter-demand at all is a judgment call. It signals that the client will not settle quietly and can improve a negotiating position, but it also commits the client to a claim they must then be prepared to bring, and an empty counter-demand is worse than none. Where the client has no counter-claim, this clause should be dropped rather than filled in weakly.
